_scope: ONLY our own English in build/translations/<slug>.json: the 't' and 'd' fields of each table entry and the values of '_chapters'. NEVER transcriptions (tables/, directory/, chronology/, toc.json), which keep the printed romanisation (CLAUDE.md hard rule, user 2026-11-28).
_rule: docs/stages/translations.md: China & Manchuria → pinyin, no tone marks, of the name as printed; Taiwan books 1895–1945 → Hepburn (pinyin); Japanese Hepburn; Korean McCune–Reischauer; personal names likewise.
_how: 'chars' = characters the source table must contain for the conversion to be safe (regex); 'alt' = other readings to check for. Add new forms here as they are met; check.py and convert.py read this file. Survey of non-China volumes: find entries whose SOURCE prints Chinese/Manchurian place characters (title, rows, columns — not notes) and list the English words they use; that found the Korea Nenkan 1926 Jiandao forms.

keep.Manchukuo: state name; English form kept (Manchoukuo/Manchou → Manchukuo, in conversions)
keep.Kwantung: 關東州 and its institutions (user 2026-11-28, overriding pinyin): the territory always as the full phrase 'Kwantung Leased Territory' (also for bare 關東州, 'Kwantung Territory', 'Kwantung Province'); institutions 'Kwantung Bureau' (關東局), 'Kwantung Government' (關東廳), 'Kwantung Army' (關東軍) etc. Dalian 大連 and Lüshun 旅順 stay pinyin only. Never confuse with Kwangtung 廣東 → Guangdong.

terms.Hsien / hsien (縣): county / counties (user 2026-11-28); rewrite phrase by phrase for singular/plural — convert.py HSIEN list. 'Kiangning Hsien' → 'Jiangning County'; 'Hsien-run' → 'County-run'.
terms.江海關: Jianghai Customs (Shanghai) — an earlier translation wrongly said 'Kiangsu Customs'

false_hits.mien-hsien: 麵線 noodles (taiwan-tokei-1938) — not 縣; leave
false_hits.Koh: Koh Kong (Cambodia) and the Taiwan land unit 甲 kō — not Chinese
false_hits.Shina: a substring of Shinagawa — match whole words only
false_hits.Shantung: also an English word (the fabric), so a dictionary filter drops it — search for it explicitly
false_hits.Kwa/Hsi/Tsi/Sze/Kian: fragments from partial-word patterns; always match whole words
false_hits.Korean McCune–Reischauer: P'y…, Ch'ung…, Mokp'o share Wade-Giles-style apostrophes — Korean names are never converted
false_hits.Tomun: 圖們鐵道 in Korea Nenkan 1926 ran inside Korea (會寧–潼關鎭, North Hamgyŏng) → Korean place, keep McCune–Reischauer 'Tomun'. Converted to Tumen by mistake 2026-11-28 and reverted. Same-name check: before converting a name in a Korean/Japanese/Taiwan book, confirm the place is in China/Manchuria (rows, addresses), not just that the characters match (安東 Andong, 大同 Taedong, 江西 Kangsŏ also exist in Korea).
